small_guidance:
- The conv3d (torch's cuDNN call) almost certainly dominates the 1.1 ms now that the post-conv tail is fused; tuning BLOCK_S/BLOCK_C of `_fused_norm_clamp_max_kernel` further will not move the needle. Still, fold the `x * multiplier` pre-multiply into the stats+norm kernel (skip the separate `x_mul` materialization) — that removes one full read+write of an [N,C,D,H,W]=128·16·14·30·30≈25M-element tensor.
- Merge `_stats_kernel` and `_fused_norm_clamp_max_kernel` into a single persistent per-(N,C) kernel that computes mean/var, normalizes, clamps, multiplies, and writes a partial channel-wise contribution to a per-(N,S) max buffer using `tl.atomic_max` — avoids the second global read of `x_flat`. Add `triton.autotune` over BLOCK_S∈{256,512,1024}, num_warps∈{4,8}, num_stages∈{2,3}.
- Multiplier appears twice (pre-norm and post-clamp); since norm is scale-invariant w.r.t. positive multiplier, but multiplier can be negative (sign flips inputs to mean/var — still invariant since mean/var of αx = α·mean, α²·var → normalize cancels |α|, but sign of normalized value flips). Be careful: `(αx - α·mean)/(|α|·std) = sign(α)·(x-mean)/std`. So pre-multiply effect on normalized output is just `sign(multiplier)`. Folding this into the kernel saves the entire pre-multiply pass.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.Conv3d` with a custom Triton im2col-GEMM kernel. With N=128, OC=16, OD·OH·OW=14·30·30=12600, IC·kD·kH·kW=3·27=81, this is a tiny-K GEMM where cuDNN has overhead; one program per (N, OC_tile=16, spatial_tile) with implicit im2col gather and an epilogue that adds bias and writes channels-last `[N, D, H, W, C]` should beat cuDNN here and feed the next kernel a coalesced layout.
- Fuse the entire post-conv pipeline into one kernel per (N, spatial_tile) operating on channels-last data: load all 16 channels into registers, compute per-channel mean/var via two passes over the spatial tile using shared accumulators (or use a two-stage launch where stage-1 produces stats per (N,C) and stage-2 streams), then in the same pass do `clamp((x*m - mean)*invstd, lo, hi)*m` and reduce max over the C=16 register axis to write `[N, S]`. With C=16 fitting in one BLOCK_C, the channel loop disappears.
- Alternative single-pass design: since C=16 is tiny, hold the entire `[C, S]` slice for one N in registers/SMEM by tiling S only; do online Welford per channel as you stream, then a second sweep does normalize+clamp+mul+max. One program per N, persistent across S tiles, eliminates the intermediate `mean`/`invstd` global tensors entirely.
